study_identification_part.si_4_title: Neurofind: using deep learning to make individualised inferences in brain-based disorders

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Outlier detection uses an adversarial autoencoder (AAE). Brain age uses linear support vector regression (SVR), which is not in the provided method list.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: The Outlier Detection model uses an adversarial auto-encoder (AAE), a deep learning approach that has shown promising results in clinical neuroimaging [42, 43].; To predict brain age, harmonised and scaled ROIrel from the train set were inputted to a linear support vector regression (SVR)

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Relative volumes of 101 cortical and subcortical regions (ROIrel) extracted from T1-weighted MRI using FreeSurfer.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: The volume of 101 cortical and subcortical regions was extracted and modelled with an adversarial autoencoder for the Outlier index model and a support vector regression for the Brain age model.; We estimated the relative brain region volumes (ROIrel ) for each subject by dividing the original brain region volumes by the total intracranial volume
nm2_2_response_variable.location: Vieira2025.pdf.md: Article Open; Vieira2025.pdf.md: MRI data acquisition and pre-processing

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: AAE was conditioned on age and sex.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: age and sex were added to the model such that the AAE was conditioned to learn a latent representation whilst taking into account this information.
